key_insight: Commutator-guided local circuit repair improves low-energy arrival in shallow quantum circuits, but does not establish quantum advantage.
engineering_relevance: Under fixed depth and evaluation budgets, improving circuit trainability alone may not deliver the desired low-energy states.
method: Build a restricted pool of local Pauli rotations from low-order host–Hamiltonian commutators and fixed same-support companion axes.
Select a compact completion layer using predeclared selectors.
evidence_signal: Across 189 paired six-qubit trials, unrepaired circuits had 0 strict successes, versus 109 for a non-deployable per-trial control envelope and 133 and 127 for two predeclared repair selectors.
watch_item: Benefits are problem- and size-dependent: repair loses to matched controls for transverse-field Ising, is weak for pure-ZZ MaxCut, and remains size-limited for weighted MIS; classical accessibility also limits advantage claims.
paper_title: Commutator-guided repair and classical-accessibility boundaries for shallow quantum circuits
